title: Ascension, the Right Hand and the New Name
english: “…to bring you up out of your graves, My people; and I will put breath in you, and you will live” (Ezekiel 37:13-14).

86. That He will go up into the heavens. David says in the 47th Psalm, “God went up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet” (Psalm 47:5). And Amos says, “He who builds His ascent into heaven” (Amos 9:6).

87. That He Himself was the one who preached. Isaiah says, “The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He has anointed Me; He has sent Me to bring good news to the poor, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to proclaim a year acceptable to the Lord and a day of recompense for our God” (Isaiah 61:1-2). And again, “My people will know My name on that day, that I Myself am the one who speaks. I am here, like one fair among the fair, like one who announces the good news of peace, making your salvation heard” (Isaiah 52:6-7).

88. That His name is in all the earth. Zechariah says, “And all who are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year by year to worship the Lord Almighty” (Zechariah 14:16). And Ezekiel says, “I will cleanse you, and I will put My Spirit within you” (Ezekiel 36:25, 27). And again, “I will give them another heart, and I will give them a new spirit” (Ezekiel 11:19). And David says in the 19th Psalm, “His voice went out into all the earth, and His words to the ends of the world” (Psalm 19:4). And Jeremiah says, “I will give them another way and another heart, to fear Me all their days” (Jeremiah 32:39).

89. That He took His seat at the right hand of the Father not from the time He ascended, but even before that. Isaiah says, “I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up” (Isaiah 6:1). And David says in the 93rd Psalm, “Your throne is prepared, Lord, even from of old; You are from everlasting” (Psalm 93:2). And again he says in the 110th, “The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet” (Psalm 110:1). And Isaiah says, “Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet” (Isaiah 66:1).

90. That we shall be called Christians. Isaiah says, “Nations will see your glory, and all kings your righteousness; and you will be called by the new name, which the Lord will name” (Isaiah 62:2). And again, “But those who serve Me will be called by a new name, which will be blessed on the earth” (Isaiah 65:15-16).

91. That the marking on the forehead was also foretold. David says in the 60th Psalm, “You have given those who fear You a mark, to flee from before the bow” (Psalm 60:4). And Isaiah says, “Those who are sealed will be made manifest, so as to learn the law” (Isaiah 8:16). And Ezekiel says, “The Lord said to the man clothed in the long robe, Put the mark on the foreheads of the men who groan and are in anguish over all the iniquities; and go through the middle of Jerusalem…” (Ezekiel 9:4).

translator_notes: The section opens with the end of Ezekiel 37:13-14, begun at the close of the previous section, and ends in the middle of Ezekiel 9:4, which the next section continues.

In this section the Psalm numbers in the running text follow the English numbering; Epiphanius’s Greek numbers are one lower (18, 109, 59). At 86.1 and 89.2 the printed numbers (40 and 2) have each lost a digit; the verses are Greek Psalms 46:6 and 92:2, Psalms 47:5 and 93:2 in English.
Heading 89 is the reading of the body of the work; in the chapter list the words “but even before that” are displaced after heading 90.
88.2 joins Ezekiel 36:25 and 36:27; 88.3 is Ezekiel 11:19 (“another heart”).
91.3: the Greek of Ezekiel 9:2-4 has “the long robe” where English Bibles, following the Hebrew, have “linen”.

title: Baptism, the Second Coming and the Judgment
english: “…and strike, and do not spare, and do not pity; the old man and the young man, the women, the nursing infants: wipe them all out; but do not come near any who bear My sign” (Ezekiel 9:5-6).

92. That baptism in Christ was foretold. Isaiah says, “Wash yourselves, become clean; remove the wickedness from your souls before My eyes” (Isaiah 1:16). And again, more plainly, “On that day God will shine forth in counsel with glory upon the earth, to exalt and glorify what is left of Israel in Zion and what is left in Jerusalem; for all who are written for life in Jerusalem will be called holy. For the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and He will cleanse the blood of Jerusalem from their midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning. And He will come, and a cloud will overshadow by day every place of Mount Zion and all that is around it” (Isaiah 4:2-5). And the baptism of the Jews according to the law also bears witness.

93. That the second coming was foretold. Malachi says, “Behold, the Lord Almighty is coming; and who will endure the day of His coming? Or who will stand at His appearing? For He will come in like a refiner’s fire, and He will sit refining and purifying” (Malachi 3:1-3). And again he says, “I will bring you to judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, against the adulteresses, and against those who swear falsely by My name” (Malachi 3:5).

94. That He will judge the world, and that judgment will be given to Him. David says in the 96th Psalm, “The Lord will judge the world in righteousness” (Psalm 96:13). And Joel says, “I will bring all the nations, and I will enter into judgment with them” (Joel 3:2). “And before Him will be a consuming fire, and behind Him a blazing flame; and behind Him a plain of desolation” (Joel 2:3). And again he says, “Before His face peoples will be crushed” (Joel 2:6). And again he says, “For the Lord has a case against His people” (Micah 6:2). And Daniel says, “I was watching in the vision of the night, and behold, One like a Son of Man was coming with the clouds of heaven, and He came as far as the Ancient of Days; and to Him were given the dominion and the honor and the kingdom, and all peoples, tribes, and tongues will serve Him; His authority is an everlasting authority” (Daniel 7:13-14). And David says in the 2nd Psalm, “The Lord said to Me, You are My Son; today I have begotten You. Ask of Me, and I will give You the nations for Your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for Your possession” (Psalm 2:7-8). And again the same says in the 76th Psalm, “The earth feared and was still when God rose up for judgment, to save the meek of the earth; for the thought of man…” (Psalm 76:8-10).
translator_notes: The section opens with the end of Ezekiel 9:5-6, begun at the close of the previous section, and ends in the middle of Psalm 76:10, which the next section completes.

In this section the Psalm numbers in the running text follow the English numbering; at 94.7 the Greek number is 75. At 94.1 the printed “5th” has lost a digit and stands for Greek Psalm 95, Psalm 96 in English.
94.2: the edition’s “I will come” is read as “I will bring”, close to the Greek of Joel 3:2 (Greek 4:2), “I will gather”.
94.4: introduced as another saying of Joel, but the words are Micah 6:2; the citation gives Micah.

title: Signs of the End and the Endless Kingdom
english: “…will give praise to You” (Psalm 76:10).

95. That the sun and the moon will be darkened. Joel says, “I will show wonders in the heaven above and on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke; and the sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes; and it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved” (Joel 2:30-32). And again he says, “The day of the Lord is at hand, for near is a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist” (Joel 2:1-2). And the Preacher says, “Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and put away anger from your heart, and remember Him who created you, before the days of your evil come, before the sun and the moon and the stars are darkened, and those who look out through the windows grow dim” (Ecclesiastes 11:9-10; 12:1-3).

96. That the heavens will be rolled up. Isaiah says, “And the heaven will be rolled up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like leaves from a vine, and as leaves fall from a fig tree” (Isaiah 34:4). And David says in the 102nd Psalm, “In the beginning You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the works of Your hands; they will perish, but You will remain; and they will all grow old like a garment, and like a cloak You will roll them up, and they will be changed” (Psalm 102:25-26). And again Isaiah says, “Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away” (Matthew 24:35; compare Isaiah 51:6).

97. That the Antichrist will come before the coming of Christ. Daniel says, “After them another king will arise, who will surpass in evils all who were before him; and he will speak words against the Most High” (Daniel 7:24-25).
98. That he will kill many. Daniel says, “I was watching, and that horn was making war with the saints” (Daniel 7:21).
99. That then there will be a time of tribulation. Daniel says, “Then there will be a time of tribulation, such tribulation as there had not been among men until then” (Daniel 12:1).

100. That Christ will come after him, and how He will come. Zechariah says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds, and the tribes will mourn, tribe by tribe” (Matthew 24:30; compare Zechariah 12:10-12). And David says in the 50th Psalm, “Our God, and He will not keep silent; fire will blaze before Him, and around Him a mighty storm” (Psalm 50:3).

101. That the sign of Christ will be plain to see. Isaiah says, “Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear; and when He has gathered them, He will not judge by appearance, nor will He convict by hearsay” (Matthew 24:30; Isaiah 11:3).

102. That the kingdom will have no end. Daniel says, “His kingdom will not be destroyed, and it will not be left to another people” (Daniel 7:14; 2:44). And David says in the 45th Psalm, “Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever” (Psalm 45:6). And again the same says in the 102nd, “But You are the same, and Your years will not fail” (Psalm 102:27).

translator_notes: The section opens with the end of Psalm 76:10, begun at the close of the previous section.
In this section the Psalm numbers in the running text follow the English numbering; Epiphanius’s Greek numbers are one lower (101, 49, 44).
The Greek numerals for 90 have fallen out of headings 95-99, and heading 96 has lost its numeral entirely; the numbers follow the sequence.

Three sayings are kept under the names the author gives but cited to their true sources: 96.3 (“Isaiah”) is Matthew 24:35 (compare Isaiah 51:6); 100.1 (“Zechariah”) is Matthew 24:30 with Zechariah 12:10-12; 101.1 (“Isaiah”) is Matthew 24:30 joined to Isaiah 11:3.
